newsitem.title: LEBANON: Scandal makes Lebanon change accounting system.
newsitem.headline: Scandal makes Lebanon change accounting system.

text.p: Lebanon's finance ministry will ditch its centuries-old accounting system and adopt modern methods following embezzlement of more than $2 million by a ministry official, the acting finance minister said on Friday.

"We have devised a new accounting system to start operation at the beginning of January as the old system did not allow effective supervision and real control over public funds," Fouad Siniora told a news conference.
"Up to now, Lebanon is still using the accounting method used before the 15th century," he said.
The new system would be applied to all public institutions and municipalities, Siniora added.

He said a junior ministry official named Rafa'at Sleiman who was responsible for issuing revenue stamps had embezzled 3.8 billion Lebanese pounds ($2.4 million) from the sale of forged and genuine stamps.
The ministry had recovered funds equalling the embezzled amount from Sleiman's assets but Sleiman was still at large and an alleged accomplice is under arrest, Siniora added.
A prosecutor who charged six people in October including Sleiman with embezzling funds from the sale of forged and genuine stamps put the amount at 15 billion pounds.

Siniora dismissed press reports that 40 billion pounds were embezzled, saying two international auditing firms had confirmed the conclusion of Central Inspection Agency investigators that the amount was 3.8 billion.
